subject: Tiered prepay credit amortization and annual allocation questions
messages:
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@orbitai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbitai.com; cfo@orbitai.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on multi-year prepay / drawdown mechanics

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood's latency profile but procurement has a few follow-ups on the prepay model before we can present to the finance committee. High level asks:

- We expect to sign a 36-month contract but would prefer to prepay annually (three annual prepayments) rather than a single up-front amount. Can Redwood amortize credits across the term while allowing us to draw against a prepay "wallet"?
- We need a ramp schedule for the first 12 months (we expect usage to be 40% of committed tokens in Q1, 70% in Q2, 100% thereafter). How would discounts and credit allocation change across those ramped months?
- What happens to unused credits at year boundaries? Are rollovers allowed? If so, any cap?
- If we underuse vs commit, what's the true-up process and timing?
- For termination or conversion to Dedicated later, what’s the refund / credit transfer policy?

Can you send a short one-pager + example amortization table? Procurement wants numbers (monthly burn examples) to compare against other offers.

Best,
Emma
Procurement, OrbitAI

P.S. We'll likely involve our CFO in the final pricing call (cc'd).

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@orbitai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on multi-year prepay / drawdown mechanics

Hi Emma — great questions, thanks for laying them out clearly. Below is a concise proposal and I attached a sample amortization workbook that mirrors the figures. Happy to walk through live.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Contract: 36-month term, invoiced as three annual prepayments (one invoice per 12-month year).
- Discounts: tiered by committed annual spend; baseline discount of 18% on list for Year 1, increases to 22% for Year 2, and 25% for Year 3 for a stepped incentive on multi-year commitment.
- Wallet & drawdown: Each annual prepay creates a wallet for that 12-mo year. Usage is debited from the active year's wallet in real-time (per token). Unspent credits at year-end can rollover up to 10% of that year's prepay into the next year (one-time carryover), capped and expiring after the next 12 months.
- Ramp schedule: We can front-load credit release if needed: by default the wallet equals the annual prepay amount; if you expect Q1=40% of expected annual run-rate, we can allocate a quarterly sub-bucket so reporting shows expected vs actual and allow automated rebalancing.
- True-up: Quarterly reconciliation. If actual usage < 90% of committed quarterly allocation, we do a one-time adjustment at quarter close (either credit carryforward allowance or an invoice credit). If actual usage > committed by more than 15% we apply overage pricing at the agreed overage rate (list minus 5%).
- Termination / conversion: On early termination, unused wallet balance is refundable pro-rata minus a minimum term protection equal to one quarter's committed spend. If converting to Dedicated, remaining credits can be applied toward first quarter of Dedicated usage (technical and compliance review pending).

I'll attach the workbook (RDW-OrbitAI-Proposal-v2.xlsx) with two amortization scenarios: conservative ramp and accelerated ramp. If that looks OK I can update numbers to match OrbitAI's internal forecasts and send a redlineable term sheet.

Best,
Soojin Lee

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: FW: Questions on multi-year prepay / drawdown mechanics

Soojin — quick internal note before we finalize the workbook figures. A couple of askables from Finance/RevOps:

1) Reduce rollover cap to 6% instead of 10% (we've seen credit arbitrage at larger rollovers).
2) Make the default overage rate equal to list price (no discount) for first 30 days post-commit overage, then tier down to list-5% if sustained.
3) Add a clause that allows Redwood to re-evaluate discount tiers if aggregated usage across all OrbitAI entities materially exceeds baseline (we should not commit unboundedly).

If legal signs off we'll push these into the next revision and flag the conversion carry vs refund policy for the legal checklist.

—Marissa

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@orbitai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on multi-year prepay / drawdown mechanics

Emma — quick update after an internal review (attached workbook v2 reflects these changes). Key adjustments per internal feedback:

- Rollover cap: 6% of the annual prepay (one-year carry only).
- Overage treatment: List price for first 30 days of overage, then list-5% for any sustained overage beyond that window.
- True-up cadence: Quarterly reconciles remain, but we'll add an automated weekly ledger export you can consume.

Example (from the workbook):
- Year 1 prepay: $2.4M (represents committed spend at a 20% blended effective discount).
- Monthly amortization shows Q1 at 40% ramp (months 1–3 scaled) which consumes ~36% of Year 1 wallet by the end of month 3 under conservative case.
- If by Q2 the run-rate reaches 70%, the quarterly true-up will reallocate a portion of Year 2 prepay as a provisional allowance so you avoid immediate overage charges mid-quarter.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call with you and Liam (CFO) next week to walk finance through the workbook? I have availability Wed/Thu morning PST.

Thanks,
Soojin

Soojin/Marissa — high level from a finance POV: the approach is reasonable but we need clarity on two things before we can recommend to the board:

1) How refunds are calculated on early termination (formula and timing). The one-quarter minimum protection is OK but please provide a sample calculation.
2) Treatment of taxes and foreign withholding (we operate in EU and APAC subsidiaries).

If you can add those clarifications to the next workbook/tab we can move to a term-sheet review. Also include the DocuSign flow and payment terms (net 30 vs net 45).

—Liam

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on multi-year prepay / drawdown mechanics

Liam/Emma — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. I updated the attached workbook (RDW-OrbitAI-Proposal-v2.xlsx) and added a "Refund & Tax" tab that shows the sample early-termination calculation and options for tax handling by region. Summary:

- Early termination refund: Refund = unspent wallet balance - pro-rated minimum protection (one quarter of committed annual spend) - outstanding invoices. Refunds issued within 45 days of termination notice.
- Cross-border taxes: We will include a line-item for any withholding taxes; Redwood will provide invoice-level documentation and work with customer tax contacts on gross-up options if required.
- Payment terms: Defaults to Net 30 for US entities. For EU/APAC subsidiaries we can support Net 45 on request subject to credit review.

Next steps: I can send a redline-able term sheet and DocuSign link once you confirm which amortization scenario (conservative vs accelerated) you prefer. I've attached both scenario tabs and a CSV with monthly amortization.

Attachments: RDW-OrbitAI-Proposal-v2.xlsx, Prepay-Allocation-Calc.csv

Looking forward to the call — I'll propose Wed 08/25 10:00 AM PST and will update if that conflicts.
